title: Offline-capable zero-trust policy, key and replication enforcement for tagged data at the tactical edge (ZT Data Pillar under DDIL)
scoring_note: Scores are analytical heuristics, not facts. Labels: FACT / INFERENCE / HYPOTHESIS with confidence HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW. New fact this session: the Army T-ICAM OTA prototype vendor is Akamai (Breaking Defense, 2024-04, https://breakingdefense.com/2024/04/army-picks-akamai-for-prototype-battlefield-zero-trust-project-t-icam/ - FACT, HIGH); the same search found no funded PEO solicitation or award for a tactical ZT data-pillar/edge key-release capability beyond the DUCES RFI (2025-02) and Navy SBIR topics N244-P03 (2024) and DON26BZ03-NV059 (2026) - Public evidence insufficient for any production pull.

scores.rationale: FACT/HIGH: the Army CTO authorizing official rated the NGC2 prototype 'very high risk' because any user could see all data with no logging (CNBC 2025-10-03); Balikatan 2026 still needed JICOs/FDOs hand-tagging releasability after 8+ years (DVIDS 2026-05); WFX 24-03 regenerated Secret products by hand (MIPB 2025). Severe for the authorizing official and the FDO, but units keep operating on implicit trust, so it is not mission-stopping for the S6 - hence 4 not 5.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: every disconnection event at a hub/spoke node and every coalition data exchange re-triggers the trade-off (implicit trust vs. unreadable objects, manual re-tagging); Ivy Mass / Ivy Sting deliberately test denied-network operation (army.mil 2026; E03-F9), so the pain recurs in every NGC2 exercise and daily in coalition enclaves.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH: the only money aimed at this capability is research-sized: DUCES is a sources-sought RFI with no award (Breaking Defense 2025-02; no follow-on found 2026-09), and Navy SBIR topics N244-P03 (2024) and DON26BZ03-NV059 (Phase I up to $315k, closed 2026-07-22). Adjacent NGC2 money (~$2.95B FY26 request, 50% obligation cap under FY26 NDAA - FNN 2026-02) and the CDAO Edge Data Mesh OTA ($100M, DefenseScoop 2024-12-03) are ceilings/portfolios controlled by primes, not lines this product bills against. No dedicated line: Public evidence insufficient. Not 0 because the SBIR topics are real, dated, funded asks.

FACT/HIGH (13 CFR 121.702): the primary vehicle (Army/Navy SBIR) requires >50% U.S.-citizen/PR ownership and control, which a two-founder cap table with one non-U.S. person fails until restructured with counsel; NGC2 entry is via prime subcontract (Anduril/Lockheed-Raft) at the prime's discretion; CSO/OTA and a C5ISR CRADA are open but slow and unfunded at start (E04-F2, E07-F28). Accessible in principle, gated in practice.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: open baselines exist (OpenTDF KAS/attribute services, TAK federation, production CRDT tooling) so an offline PDP/KAS with time-boxed grants and a label-aware sync filter is buildable; but offline revocation under partition is a bounded-staleness trade-off rather than a solved problem, and NSA-approved crypto integration (FY26 NDAA condition) and FIPS-validated modules are outside a small team's reach without cleared partners.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the card's own PoC estimate ($150-300k for two founders plus a contract cryptographer for 6 months) consumes the entire founder capital and yields only an unaccredited synthetic-data demo; the next milestone ($1-2.5M credible military demo) is 4-10x the available capital. Only the non-crypto label-aware sync library fits inside $250k.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a two-laptop lab demo (cut link, show policy-correct deny/allow, three-node partition convergence) is 3-6 months away; a demo a program office would credit needs DoD PKI test integration, an exercise slot (Cyber Quest, T-REX, Ivy Sting) and cATO packaging, which the card puts at 12-18 months and $1-2.5M - slow relative to gaps that can demo on public data alone.

FACT/HIGH for the MVP: OpenTDF spec, ATAK-CIV/CoT schemas and the STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 label syntaxes are public (some registration required), so synthetic tagged messages are fully obtainable. Real labeled operational data and government attribute feeds are classified/CUI, only reachable inside a sponsored experiment with cleared U.S.-person staff - the non-U.S.-person founder should assume no access.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH (constraints, not legal conclusions): the core differentiator (delegated key release/revocation) is cryptographic key-management software, export-controlled under EAR Category 5 Part 2 at minimum and possibly ITAR USML XI/XIII if specially designed for military use; the Indonesian founder cannot be assumed able to write or review that code without a deemed-export license/technology control plan; NSA-approved high-assurance encryption and classified attribute data require cleared U.S. persons and possibly a facility clearance with FOCI mitigation (32 CFR 117.11 treats even a permanent resident as a foreign interest); production requires an ATO/cATO. Only the SBIR-free OT/CSO route and an EAR99-style non-crypto core avoid the worst of this. Counsel required at every step.

FACT/HIGH: the MVP is fully unclassified (commercial laptops, OpenTDF, ATAK-CIV, synthetic US-only/REL FVEY/REL NATO messages). Deducted because the card rates classification dependence 'eventually' and the first government-furnished attribute feeds, exercise networks and NSA crypto integration arrive early on the credible-demo path, at which point one founder is walled off.

FACT (claims exist)/MEDIUM: no vendor publicly documents the full seam (offline PDP + delegated key release + label-aware convergent replication), but every adjacent piece is held by funded players: Virtru/OpenTDF (format owner, offline TDF and Multi-KAS claims), Xage ($1.5M Navy PMW 790 Phase II 2024-10; $17M Space Force 2023-09), Anduril+Booz Allen ('zero trust' on Lattice/Menace, BusinessWire 2026-05-18), Palantir Foundry ABAC, Raft, Ditto (STRATFI up to $28M), Akamai (T-ICAM), CDS vendors (Everfox-Virtru ACP-240 partnership 2025-10-16). Absence of an exact competitor is not evidence of opportunity.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: the Army CTO memo proves the leading prime shipped a prototype without access control (2025-09), and the Army's stated preference for government-owned NGC2 APIs (army.mil 2026-06-22) creates a vendor-neutral seam primes dislike filling for each other. But the same prime announced a bundled ZT fix eight months later, Virtru can add an edge KAS, and the Army can declare cached identity plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level' - the incumbents' cheapest response is to absorb, and they have the money and cleared staff to do so.

FACT/HIGH on interfaces: TAK Server/ATAK-CIV and OpenTDF are open and government- or community-controlled, which is favorable; but the product must also sit inside proprietary meshes (Lattice Mesh, Raft federation, Ditto), federate with Army EICAM/T-ICAM (Akamai) and Naval Identity Service, and hand off to accredited CDS at boundaries (NSA/NCDSMO controlled). Label schemas differ across ISM/CAPCO, STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240. The card lists 'integration complexity' and 'proprietary incumbent architecture' as reasons the gap is unsolved.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: defensibility exists only if a government sponsor treats the component as the accredited reference implementation (ATO artifacts, FIPS build, embedded in TAK/NGC2 baseline) - the OpenTDF-style position. The open ZTDF format is deliberately non-proprietary and the label-aware merge algorithm is publishable; without sponsor adoption the card itself concludes 'it is a feature primes copy'.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: offline attribute-based key release and policy-aware sync map to sovereign/OT/maritime/mining/disaster-response disconnected-sync markets and OpenTDF already has commercial users via Virtru; but commercial buyers rarely need multi-releasability convergence, so the dual-use product competes on Ditto's and Xage's turf, not on defense-specific features.

HYPOTHESIS/LOW-MEDIUM: if a reference edge policy/key node were adopted it could extend across Army NGC2 nodes, Navy expeditionary sites, coalition MPE enclaves and NATO data-centric security (STANAG 4774/4778 are allied by construction; Germany D-LBO/TaWAN 2026-2029 needs label-aware edge data services); but each expansion runs through a different prime and accreditation regime, and a U.S. NSA-crypto build cannot simply be exported.

INFERENCE/MEDIUM: a fielded edge KAS/PDP would be licensed and sustained per node/unit with recurring accreditation and policy-update work, which is genuinely recurring revenue; but the most likely commercial form is a component priced inside a prime's NGC2 or Navy vehicle, so the recurring revenue accrues via subcontract at the prime's margin.

Score of 1 explained - FACT/HIGH on the constraints, INFERENCE on fit: the card marks four roles fatal-if-absent (applied cryptographer, CRDT distributed-systems engineer, cleared U.S.-person ZT/ICAM/labeling SME, export/immigration counsel) and states neither founder can fill the cleared-SME role; the crypto core is the export-controlled surface the Indonesian founder must be assumed unable to touch; the German founder is clearance-eligible only after naturalization (roughly 2031 at the earliest) and remains a FOCI 'foreign interest' as a permanent resident (32 CFR 117.11); SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) fails on a 50/50 split. A 'strong engineer' is not, by default, an applied cryptographer or CRDT specialist, and the business founder has no documented DoD ZT network. The only part of the product the team can legally build alone is the part with the least moat.

market.summary: No program office owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name and no budget line exists; every dollar found is research money (DUCES RFI with no award 19 months on; two Navy SBIR cycles at Phase I scale); primes will bundle ZT into Lattice/Menace at zero incremental price and the Army can accept cached identity plus enclave plus CDS as target-level compliance; label-schema and mesh fragmentation push a small vendor toward bespoke integration work; the cleared-SME and export-control walls make the team's only path a services model its $250k cannot fund. Assessment: the strongest of the three; every load-bearing claim traces to the card's own evidence and was not contradicted by this session's search.

competition.summary: Virtru already advertises Multi-KAS / Private Keystore with disconnected and air-gapped TDF operation (vendor claim, tier 4); Booz Allen reports ZT logging/policy enforcement 'live' on Anduril Menace/Lattice (press release 2026-05-18); Raft, Ditto and Lattice Mesh already do DDIL convergence and can add policy filters incrementally; Palantir has mature ABAC; production money flows through incumbent vehicles. Assessment: partly overstated - none of the cited announcements documents label-aware convergent replication across releasability tiers or fielding at tactical echelon, and vendor marketing is not proof a product works - but the direction is correct: the format owner and the mesh owners are the natural home for this feature, and they have cleared staff the founders lack.

feasibility.summary: Xage, funded and Navy/Space Force-contracted, has not closed the full gap in 2-3 years; DUCES has not converted to an acquisition; three fatal-if-absent roles are unfilled and the core crypto is legally inaccessible to one founder; SBIR ownership fails on a 50/50 split and an outside raise worsens it; the capital ladder ($150-300k PoC, $1-2.5M credible demo, $5-12M production) outstrips $250k by 4-10x at the first credible milestone; offline revocation under partition is an unresolved trade-off. Assessment: accurate on eligibility and capital; the 'unresolved CAP trade-off' point is weaker (bounded staleness is an acceptable engineering answer that OpenTDF-style grants already use), but the founder-fit and capital arguments stand.

verdict_rationale: Three skeptics refute at strength 4 and, on the evidence, they are right about the two things that decide this gap for these founders. (1) The PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE chain breaks at the fourth link and never recovers: the problem and users are real and dated (Army CTO memo 2025-09 via CNBC 2025-10-03; Balikatan 2026; WFX 24-03), the requirement owner is only an INFERENCE (Army G-6/DoD CIO ZT PfMO), no program office owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name (Public evidence insufficient), the contracting office is an INFERENCE, the budget line does not exist (only DUCES, an RFI with no award as of 2026-09, and Navy SBIR Phase I topics), and the only vehicles are SBIR topics the team is not eligible for on a 50/50 cap table (13 CFR 121.702) or a prime subcontract the prime has every incentive to withhold. The major penalty for a broken chain applies in full. This session's one verification search confirmed the picture: T-ICAM went to Akamai under an OTA in 2024-04 (identity pillar only) and nothing funded has appeared for the data pillar since. (2) Founder fit is 2.0 with two criteria at 1: the product's only defensible component - delegated offline key release and revocation - is the export-controlled crypto surface that the Indonesian founder must be assumed unable to build or review, the cleared U.S.-person ZT/labeling SME is fatal-if-absent and unfillable by either founder before roughly 2031, and the $150-300k PoC consumes all founder capital while the first credible milestone costs $1-2.5M. Market attractiveness is 2.6 on the team-independent criteria, which by itself would argue 'borderline' for a cleared U.S. team with a cryptographer; combined with a broken procurement chain and a founder-fit of 2.0 it is a kill for this team. The narrower versions the skeptics propose (a no-crypto label-aware sync filter, or an FDO releasability-tagging tool, EU-domiciled) are not G02: once the key/policy/revocation core is removed, what remains is a feature that Raft, Ditto, Anduril, Virtru or the TAK Product Center can add in a sprint, and its buyer is the coalition-tagging problem that GAO-25-106454 (2025-04-08) says no DoD entity owns and that DISA says stays network-centric until about 2027. That derivative belongs with the coalition-interoperability gap in the registry and should be evaluated there, not credited to G02. What would reverse this verdict: a funded PEO C3T / PMW 790 solicitation or production award naming edge key release / policy-aware replication with a dollar figure; a public program-office finding that the Booz Allen-Anduril or Virtru offerings fail label-aware convergence; or the team adding a cleared U.S.-person cryptographer as a co-founder with a compliant cap table.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not applicable (verdict is kill). For the record, the only survivable derivative all three skeptics converge on is: drop key custody, offline KAS and all controlled cryptography; build an open-source, EAR99-candidate (counsel to confirm) label-aware sync/filter library for TAK federation and OpenTDF policy metadata using STANAG 4774/4778 and ACP-240 labels, aimed at the documented FDO/JICO hand-tagging workflow (Balikatan 2026, WFX 24-03), domiciled in a NATO nation for DIANA eligibility and Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN subcontract chain (Rheinmetall/blackned, delivery 2026-2029). That is a feature-sized wedge with no identified budget owner on either side of the Atlantic and should be scored under the coalition releasability/interoperability gap rather than under G02.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, the only thing they could legally and affordably build first is the non-crypto half: an open-source label-aware sync filter and offline policy-decision sidecar for TAK Server / ATAK-CIV that reads OpenTDF policy metadata and STANAG 4774/4778 / ACP-240 labels and decides, deterministically and with provenance, which tagged objects a partitioned node may store and forward, with three laptops emulating US-only, REL FVEY and REL NATO nodes over a tens-of-kbit/s emulated link; they would show it to the DEVCOM C5ISR ESI Directorate (the DUCES RFI author), the DoD CIO ZT PfMO interoperable-data-tagging team, and the Raft / Anduril data-layer leads on NGC2, and the demonstration would prove zero unauthorized reads across partitions (fuzzed), convergence without manual de-duplication, and bandwidth overhead low enough for a tactical radio. The customer would care because the Army CTO memo said 'we cannot control who sees what' and Balikatan 2026 still hand-tags releasability, so a measurable, standards-anchored answer to those two findings is attractive on its face. But this is exactly where it fails: the demo does not include the piece that makes the product a product - delegated offline key release and revocation - because that piece is export-controlled crypto one founder cannot touch and a FIPS/NSA-approved build the team cannot afford; without it, what they have shown is a replication filter, which Raft, Ditto, Anduril or the TAK Product Center can copy in weeks once a sponsor signals interest, and Virtru can pair with its own KAS. An incumbent does not need to crush them; it needs only to add a policy hook to its merge function and let the Army declare cached identity plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level'. The milestone that would justify $2-5M - a named program office (PEO C3T CPE C2IN or PMW 790) funding an OTA or Phase II specifically for an edge KAS/PDP component, with a cleared U.S.-person cryptographer on the founding team and a SBIR-compliant or OT-based path - does not exist on public evidence as of 2026-09-25, and the founders cannot create it with $250k. That is why the gap fails for this team even though the pain is real.
bear_case_summary: Real, dated pain (Army CTO memo 2025-09; Balikatan 2026; WFX 24-03; DUCES RFI; two Navy SBIR cycles) but no program office, no budget line, no funded solicitation 19 months after the only Army RFI, primes bundling 'zero trust' into Lattice/Menace for free (2026-05-18) and Virtru claiming offline/Multi-KAS TDF, an Army that can declare cached identity (Akamai T-ICAM) plus enclave plus CDS 'target-level', a crypto core that is export-controlled and legally inaccessible to one founder, three unfillable fatal roles, SBIR ineligibility on a 50/50 cap table, and a capital ladder ($1-2.5M then $5-12M) that outstrips $250k by an order of magnitude at the first credible milestone. The likeliest outcome is absorption, not purchase.
bull_case_summary: The seam is genuinely unclaimed: no vendor publicly documents an offline policy decision point plus delegated key release plus label-aware convergent replication, and none is evidenced as fielded at tactical echelon; the DoD ZT target-level deadline (2027-09-30), NSA ZIGs (2026-01) naming ZTDF/IC-TDF (per Virtru, 2026-04, MEDIUM), the FY26 NDAA tying NGC2 money to DDIL resiliency and NSA-approved crypto, the Army's stated wish for government-owned NGC2 APIs (2026-06-22) and the DUCES/Navy SBIR asks all point the same way; OpenTDF and TAK give a small team open baselines; and the coalition version of the pain (GAO-25-106454, STANAG 4774/4778, ACP-240) is allied by construction, so an EU-domiciled entity has a NATO DIANA / D-LBO route. A cleared U.S. team with an applied cryptographer, entering via a C5ISR CRADA and an NGC2 prime subcontract, could plausibly become the accredited reference edge policy/key node - but that team is not these two founders.

chain_check.problem: FACT/HIGH - enforcement vs. availability at disconnection; Army CTO memo, Balikatan 2026, WFX 24-03
chain_check.user: FACT/HIGH - battalion/brigade S6 and data managers, NGC2 node operators, coalition FDOs/JICOs
chain_check.requirement_owner: INFERENCE/MEDIUM - Army G-6/CIO (Unified Network Plan 2.0), DoD CIO ZT PfMO; no requirement document names tactical data-pillar enforcement
chain_check.program_office: Public evidence insufficient - none owns 'tactical ZT data pillar' by name; candidates are Army CPE C2IN/PEO C3T and Navy PMW 790
chain_check.contracting_office: INFERENCE/LOW - ACC-APG or NAVWAR; no solicitation to anchor it
chain_check.budget: FACT/HIGH that none is dedicated; adjacent NGC2 portfolio and CDAO OTA are prime-controlled ceilings, not obligations to this capability
chain_check.contract_vehicle: SBIR topics only (team ineligible on a 50/50 cap table); DUCES RFI is not a vehicle; prime subcontract at prime discretion
chain_check.chain_broken_at: PROGRAM OFFICE and BUDGET - major penalty applied

confidence_note: HIGH that G02 as framed is not a credible candidate for these two founders on 2026-09 public evidence; MEDIUM on the market-independent scores, which could rise if PEO C3T or PMW 790 issues a funded data-pillar solicitation before the 2027-09-30 ZT deadline.
